call.context: The Arabs call anything abundant; lexical prose before the numbered interpretations

lord.context: Quran quotation and hadith prose in the first river interpretation

prior_review_continuity.prior_statement_en: Al-Tha'labi reports an interpretation of al-Kawthar as miracles from the Lord by which those responding to the Prophet's call were guided.
prior_review_continuity.required_refinement: Keep al-Tha'labi as Qurtubi's named reporting source. The interpretation begins with an unnamed قيل, and al-Tha'labi's own displayed text also uses قيل, so no originating authority, personal adoption, or route may be assigned.

voice_and_claim_boundary.safe_statement_en: Al-Qurtubi gives as the twelfth interpretation an unnamed view that al-Kawthar means miracles of the Lord by which those responding to the Prophet's call were guided, and says al-Tha'labi recounted it.
voice_and_claim_boundary.context_note: Al-Qurtubi explicitly prefers the first and second interpretations; that preference does not transfer to Q04J.

thalabi_own_work_boundary.exact_witness: وقيل: معجزات أكثرت بها أهل الإجابة لدعوتك
thalabi_own_work_boundary.note: The view appears in an unattributed list. Nearby isnads belong to other reports and must not be attached to this statement.

wording_variant.qurtubi_text: معجزات الرب هدي بها أهل الإجابة لدعوتك
wording_variant.thalabi_displayed_edition_text: معجزات أكثرت بها أهل الإجابة لدعوتك
material_differences: Qurtubi includes الرب; the displayed al-Tha'labi text does not.
Qurtubi reads هدي (were guided); the displayed al-Tha'labi text reads أكثرت (were made numerous/increased).
Qurtubi assigns source-local number twelve; al-Tha'labi's list is unnumbered.
